propositions: BindingStore module (799 LOC) owns byte persistence, lifecycle policy, recovery, and rotation logic without cohesive internal boundaries, creating ownership ambiguity for new safety rules.
Production code mutates inner entry objects returned by shallow all_bindings() query, risking unintended state changes and serialization loss.

Decompose BindingStore into three internal owners (repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, recovery) behind unchanged public facade while preserving all serialization, unknown fields, and compatibility.
Durable tombstone marks retirement intent; a live binding is removed only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities all agree; explicit unretire is the sole way to revoke tombstone intent.
Interrupted retirements must be completed before remote issue fetch by exact-match repair running after staleness validation, preventing interleaving of new liveness evidence with completion.
Automatic liveness signals (404 grace, clear_absent, same-key confirm) cannot override durable tombstone; only explicit unretire removes it.
